uncited: This method addresses the problem of generalizing neural radiance field representations to unseen objects or scenes without requiring per-scene optimization.
It solves the limitation of standard NeRFs, which overfit to specific training views, by learning generalizable geometric priors from source images.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [DuDoTrans](1409-dudotrans.md) and [Transformer-based Tomographic Reconstruction](11047-transformer-based-tomographic-reconstruction.md) by focusing on cross-view feature aggregation via attention mechanisms rather than iterative tomographic inversion or specific architectural variants like Ray Transformers.
The method constructs a generalizable representation by aggregating information from multiple source views using a transformer-based attention module.
- **Outputs:** A generalizable radiance field representation capable of rendering novel views of unseen objects or scenes.
The core data structure is a feature volume or a set of view-dependent features aggregated via attention.
The specific layout depends on the implementation variant (e.g., cost volumes or feature volumes), but generally involves multi-view feature tensors aligned in 3D space.
**Feature Extraction:** Extract features from the source images using a backbone network (e.g., CNN or ViT).
**View Aggregation:** Use a transformer-based attention module to aggregate source view information.
This involves computing attention weights between query features (at a target 3D location or ray) and key/value features from the source views.
**Generalization:** The aggregated features encode geometric and appearance priors learned from the dataset, allowing the model to generalize to unseen instances.
**Rendering:** Render the novel view by querying the aggregated representation along rays.

The specific formulation for generalizable radiance fields may involve spatial attention or ray-wise attention to aggregate multi-view features.

- **Generalization Gap:** Performance may degrade on objects significantly different from the training distribution.
- **View Density:** Requires a sufficient number of source views to capture geometry accurately.
A geometry-free method using a CNN and Encoder-Decoder Transformer to produce output color for an entire ray at once.

It uses a CNN to extract feature patches from scene images, feeds patches into an Encoder-Decoder Transformer along with camera ray and viewpoint coordinates $\{o, d\}$, and produces output color by querying the entire ray at once.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of source views and the transformer architecture.
Attention mechanisms can be $O(N^2)$ in the number of views or tokens.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing features for all source views and the aggregated representation.
- **Limitations:** May require careful tuning of attention mechanisms; performance depends on the diversity and quality of the training dataset.
- **When to use:** When generalization to new objects/scenes is required without per-scene optimization.
- **When not to use:** When high-fidelity reconstruction of a specific, known scene is needed with dense input views.
This approach builds on the trend of using deep learning for 3D representation.
It specifically leverages transformer architectures to handle the non-local dependencies inherent in multi-view aggregation.
The method is part of the broader effort to make neural radiance fields more practical for real-world applications by reducing the need for extensive per-scene training.
